newsitem.title: GERMANY: MG buys back participation certificates.
newsitem.headline: MG buys back participation certificates.

text.p: Germany's Metallgesellschaft AG said on Wednesday it was buying back a further 100 million marks ($64 million) of participation certificates in a further sign that the company's balance sheet has now returned to financial health.

MG, which issued the paper to banks as part of a rescue deal when it slipped to the brink of bankruptcy in early 1994, said it was buying back a nominal 100 million marks worth of the non-convertible certificates.

MG, which originally issued 267 million marks of the paper within the framework of a 3.4 billion mark rescue package for the company, said it now had just 33.5 million marks in participation certificates outstanding.
Of the total issue -- which banks purchased at five times the nominal value -- half was convertible and half not.
MG said the convertible paper had been switched almost completely into stock by the bank holders between October 1, 1995 and October 1, 1996.

"The buy back was made possible by the good result and continued improvement of the financial position in the business year just ended," MG said in its statement. "Metallgesellschaft is starting the new year with a better balance sheet structure."
The company's pre-tax profit soared 70 percent to 290 million marks in the year to September 30, 1996.
That was its second year of recovery from the huge financial problems encountered in late 1993, when it lost billions of marks on risky oil deals in the United States.
-- Janet Northcote, Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.566 German Marks)
